architectures.label: Amyloid-production dominant
architectures.primary_hypothesis: A change in APP dosage, cleavage or secretase-dependent peptide production is the earliest dominant perturbation, with downstream soluble amyloid stress facilitating tau pathology, glial response and persistent tissue injury.
architectures.discriminating_prediction: A measurable shift in APP processing or A-beta species should precede downstream tau acceleration and damage in the subgroup assigned to this architecture; changing the upstream production pathway should alter the downstream trajectory.
falsification_criteria: Longitudinal data show tau, vascular or injury changes consistently precede the proposed APP/A-beta shift in the target subgroup.
Well-controlled perturbation of APP/A-beta production changes the biomarker but not downstream tau, synaptic or damage trajectories.
limitations: Most late-onset disease does not carry a deterministic APP or presenilin mutation.
Fluid A-beta concentration is not a direct measurement of toxic soluble oligomer exposure at synapses.

architectures.label: Amyloid-clearance dominant
architectures.primary_hypothesis: The primary vulnerability is a reduction in amyloid clearance through APOE-dependent lipid transport, endosomal-lysosomal processing, vascular transport or perivascular drainage, allowing net A-beta retention despite no necessary early increase in production.
architectures.discriminating_prediction: Measures that separate production from clearance should show impaired clearance flux preceding net amyloid retention; repair of the relevant clearance route should change later amyloid and downstream damage trajectory.
falsification_criteria: Direct or validated flux measures show normal clearance before amyloid accumulation while production is increased.
Clearance perturbation does not change A-beta retention or downstream trajectories in the relevant biological subtype.
limitations: Clearance is difficult to measure directly in living humans.
Different cellular and vascular clearance routes may dominate in different subgroups.

architectures.label: Tau / neuronal vulnerability dominant
architectures.primary_hypothesis: Cell-specific tau misprocessing or neuronal vulnerability is an early dominant driver in a subset, with tau seeding and network injury becoming partly self-sustaining and not fully dependent on contemporaneous amyloid burden.
architectures.discriminating_prediction: A reproducible subgroup should show tau-related and synaptic/circuit changes before or disproportionate to amyloid change, and tau-targeted perturbation should reduce downstream damage even when amyloid status is held constant.
falsification_criteria: In adequately powered longitudinal cohorts, tau changes consistently follow A-beta changes with no reliable tau-first subgroup.
Tau perturbation changes tau biomarkers but not downstream neuronal or accumulated-damage outcomes.
limitations: A tau-first architecture must not be inferred from cross-sectional tau associations.
Human causal perturbation evidence for tau propagation remains limited.

architectures.label: Neurovascular dominant
architectures.primary_hypothesis: Early endothelial, pericyte, blood-brain barrier, perfusion or perivascular drainage dysfunction is the dominant vulnerability, adding neuronal injury and potentially impairing amyloid clearance.
architectures.discriminating_prediction: In a defined subgroup, vascular or perfusion abnormalities should precede or independently predict later proteinopathy and persistent neuronal/neurovascular damage after major confounders and co-pathologies are handled.
falsification_criteria: High-quality longitudinal vascular measures appear only after established amyloid/tau pathology and add no independent prognostic or mechanistic information.
Targeted vascular perturbation does not modify clearance, neuronal injury or damage trajectories in relevant models.
limitations: Vascular risk is not synonymous with Alzheimer-specific initiation.
In-vivo measures poorly capture some capillary and pericyte mechanisms.

architectures.label: Immune / glial dominant
architectures.primary_hypothesis: A primary shift in microglial or astrocytic state, phagocytic capacity or inflammatory resolution is an early vulnerability that alters protein clearance, complement-mediated synaptic remodeling and tissue injury.
architectures.discriminating_prediction: Cell-state-resolved longitudinal or perturbation evidence should identify glial functional changes before the downstream injury pattern, while separating effective phagocytic clearance from damaging inflammation.
falsification_criteria: Glial state changes consistently follow pathology and do not predict independent downstream outcomes.
Selective manipulation of the proposed glial program fails to alter clearance, synaptic injury or damage in relevant human-derived systems.
limitations: Glial states are heterogeneous, region-specific and can be protective or damaging.
Peripheral inflammatory measurements do not directly observe CNS glial states.

architectures.label: Metabolic / mitochondrial dominant
architectures.primary_hypothesis: An early failure of bioenergetics, lipid handling, redox or calcium regulation reduces neuronal resilience and amplifies proteostasis failure, synaptic dysfunction and later proteinopathy in a subset.
architectures.discriminating_prediction: Cell- and region-resolved metabolic measures should change before or independently of downstream tau/synaptic injury, and restoring the implicated metabolic process should lower future damage in a perturbation model.
falsification_criteria: Metabolic signals are explained entirely by downstream neuronal loss or reduced activity.
Targeted metabolic rescue fails to alter downstream pathology or accumulated damage under validated conditions.
limitations: Metabolic dysfunction can be a cause, consequence or amplifier.
FDG-PET is not a direct assay of mitochondrial ATP production or redox flux.

architectures.label: Mixed multi-hit / threshold transition
architectures.primary_hypothesis: No single pathway is sufficient; several vulnerabilities in protein processing, immunity, vascular support and metabolism accumulate until a nonlinear threshold is crossed, after which positive feedback sustains pathology and persistent damage.
architectures.discriminating_prediction: A multi-hit model should explain heterogeneity and predict held-out transitions better than single-driver alternatives, with interpretable interactions and calibrated uncertainty rather than merely a better in-sample fit.
falsification_criteria: A simpler single-driver model consistently performs as well or better on independent cohorts and perturbation data.
The proposed interaction terms are not identifiable or fail pre-registered tests and negative controls.
limitations: Multi-hit models are prone to overfitting and post-hoc storytelling.
Complexity is not evidence; each interaction must earn inclusion through identifiability and external validation.
